quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where does debris and oil from cars collect in a traffic lane?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Where motorcycle riders should always travel for safety.
Where drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Debris and oil from cars collect in the center of the lane. Other hazards like utility hole covers are also found there.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their right leg, it signals a hazard on the right side of the road. Group riders use signals like this to communicate with each other.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on either side increases the risk of a collision. Riding far to the side might also encourage the other driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles in front of you to see farther ahead. Be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: When it is raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery when rain first starts because oil from cars has not washed away yet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is usually the safest choice.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger will sit differently due to extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, headlights, and mirrors. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking?
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Studies show that nearly 40 percent of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking. Alcohol is a major cause of deadly motorcycle accidents.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, the motorcycle's stopping distance:

options.text: Will be similar to a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be increased.
questions.explanation: Added weight increases the motorcycle's inertia and stopping distance. Start slowing and stopping earlier when carrying a load or passenger in the sidecar.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.
Keep your hand on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hand on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones, keep your hand ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: When loading cargo onto a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Pack lighter items near the front.
Try to not place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: If the road makes it hard to stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Follow the car ahead more closely.
Stay farther behind the car ahead.
Let someone else ride your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car ahead.
questions.explanation: You need more space between you and the car ahead if stopping takes longer than normal. This is important on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or in heavy traffic. Keep at least a three-second gap between you and the vehicle in front.

questions.question: To swerve correctly:

options.text: Move your body weight quickly to one side.
Push the handlegrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handlegrip opposite to the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handlegrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handlegrip on the side you want to turn toward. Push the opposite handlegrip to turn back to your original direction after you avoid the hazard.

questions.question: Before you pass another rider on the left, you should:

options.text: Move to the right part of your lane so they see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left part of your lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of your lane so they see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave back and forth in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of your lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane to see ahead better and to be more visible to drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before you change lanes.

questions.question: You must report a crash to police if:

options.text: Two or more vehicles are involved.
An animal, such as a deer, is involved.

questions.correctAnswerText: The damage is at least $1,000.
questions.explanation: If a crash causes at least $1,000 in damage, or if anyone is injured or killed, you must report it right away to local police, the sheriff's office, or the State Highway Patrol.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: The best footwear for riding a motorcycle has:
questions.correctAnswerText: Short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on surfaces. Tuck in any laces so they do not get caught.

questions.question: A rectangular sign shows:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limits.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are white with black letters or symbols and show road rules, like speed limits. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: In traffic, motorcycles need:

options.text: Much less stopping distance than cars.
The same stopping distance as cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same stopping distance as cars.
questions.explanation: In traffic, a motorcycle needs the same distance to stop as a car does.

questions.question: A passenger on a motorcycle:

options.text: Must wear a helmet if under 18 years old.
Must wear a helmet if the rider has had their license for two years or less.
Does not have to wear a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must wear a helmet if under 18 years old.
questions.explanation: Any rider or passenger under 18 must wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards. If the rider must wear a helmet, the passenger must also wear one, no matter their age. All riders should wear helmets on every ride.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while turning, you should:

options.text: Straighten the motorcycle, straighten the handlebars, then stop.
Brake hard on both brakes while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the motorcycle, straighten the handlebars, then stop.
questions.explanation: If you must stop quickly while turning, straighten the motorcycle first, then brake. If you cannot straighten the motorcycle, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually. Reduce your lean angle, then increase brake pressure as you slow down.

questions.question: What is one difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield prevents eye watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind. A windshield does not. A windshield is not a good replacement for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. It is safest to assume that any vehicle that could hit you will try to do so.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when you pull either brake lever.
It connects the front brake to the gear shifter and applies the brake when you downshift.
It connects the rear brake to a foot control.
It connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when you pull either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes on a motorcycle. When you use either brake lever, both brakes are applied. Read your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How should you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Push the handgrip in the opposite direction of your turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, push the left handgrip, then push the right to return to your normal path. To swerve right, push the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: What should you do when riding?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced while turning. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.
